CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region means Pringsewu Regency. 2. Regional Government means the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent means the Regent of Pringsewu. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary means the Regional Secretary of Pringsewu Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus in Pringsewu Regency. 7. Woman means an adult human being of female gender. 8. Child means a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence means a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim means a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence means any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women means any act of violence against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children means any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence means any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence means any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner. 17. Neglect means the act of neglecting women and or children within the scope of the household which according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence means any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women means all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 20. Law enforcement means action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid means legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Implementation of protection means a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention means direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss as a result of the actions of others. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant means a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect or recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER XI

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 5

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the region.

Article 12

Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER VI

DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government has the duty to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and  c. empowering the community to prevent acts of violence.

CHAPTER XIV

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 25

1. Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
2. PPT managers who in carrying out the task of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 12

Letter a
Sufficiently clear.

Letter b
What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain statements, declarations, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter c
Sufficiently clear.

Letter d
What is meant by "the right to continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" includes: the right to have one's rights advocated and access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship. Letter e What is meant by "the right to confidential handling" is the right of victims to have their identity kept confidential at all stages of handling by officers.

Letter f
What is meant by "the right to psychological and legal assistance" is a right that includes assistance by: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members.

Letter g
Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER X

REPORTING

Article 21

1. PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
3. The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES

Article 19

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
2. PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection which in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the protection of Women and Children.
3. The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. Forms of protection provided to victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; ore. economic.
2. The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
3. The form of legal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
4. The form of medicolegal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
5. The form of psychological protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.
6. The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER XIII

FUNDING

Article 24

1. The regional government is obliged to allocate a budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1) is adjusted to the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 17

Paragraph (1)
Letter a
Sufficiently clear.

Letter b
Sufficiently clear.

Letter c
What is meant by medicolegal is the effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.

Letter d
Sufficiently clear.

Letter e
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (3)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (4)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (5)
What is meant by "safe house" is a temporary shelter intended to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. Temporary protection is provided for a period of up to 14 (fourteen) days and can be extended according to the victim's condition. PPTs that do not have a shelter can network with PPTs that have a shelter.

What is meant by "respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights in order to uphold human dignity.

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions for any reason or in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

What is meant by "protection of women's and children's human rights" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions for any reason or in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

What is meant by "protection of women's and children's human rights" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

What is meant by "best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER X

Article 21

1. PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
3. The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss as a result of the actions of others. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant means a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. SCOPE

What is meant by "protection of women's and children's human rights" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

What is meant by "best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

Article 2

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Child victim of violence means a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim means a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence means any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women means any act of violence against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children means any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence means any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence means any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner. 17. Neglect means the act of neglecting women and or children within the scope of the household which according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence means any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women means all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 20. Law enforcement means action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid means legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Implementation of protection means a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention means direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss as a result of the actions of others. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant means a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect or recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER XI

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 5

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the region.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 12

Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 2

What is meant by "respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights in order to uphold human dignity.

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions for any reason or in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

What is meant by "protection of women's and children's human rights" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

What is meant by "best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.

CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES

Article 19

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
2. PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection which in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the protection of Women and Children.
3. The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI

DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government has the duty to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and  c. empowering the community to prevent acts of violence.

Article 20

1. Forms of protection provided to victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; ore. economic.
2. The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
3. The form of legal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
4. The form of medicolegal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
5. The form of psychological protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.
6. The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER XIV

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 25

1. Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
2. PPT managers who in carrying out the task of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

c. providing education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and  c. empowering the community to prevent acts of violence.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss as a result of the actions of others. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant means a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. CHAPTER VI

DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government has the duty to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and  c. empowering the community to prevent acts of violence.

Article 2

What is meant by "respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights in order to uphold human dignity.

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions for any reason or in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

What is meant by "protection of women's and children's human rights" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Violence against children means any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence means any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence means any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner. 17. Neglect means the act of neglecting women and or children within the scope of the household which according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence means any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women means all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 20. Law enforcement means action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid means legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Implementation of protection means a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention means direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss as a result of the actions of others. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant means a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

CHAPTER VI

DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government has the duty to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and  c. empowering the community to prevent acts of violence.

CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES

Article 19

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
2. PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection which in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the protection of Women and Children.
3. The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X

REPORTING

Article 21

1. PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
3. The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER XI

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

CHAPTER XIV

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 25

1. Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
2. PPT managers who in carrying out the task of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 5

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the region.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect or recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Article 20

1. Forms of protection provided to victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; ore. economic.
2. The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
3. The form of legal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
4. The form of medicolegal protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
5. The form of psychological protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.
6. The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Article 25

1. Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;

PPT managers who in carrying out the task of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Article 11

Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Violence means any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Legal aid means legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER VI

DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 15

1. The Regional Government has the duty to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education on anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and  c. empowering the community to prevent acts of violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region means Pringsewu Regency. 2. Regional Government means the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent means the Regent of Pringsewu. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary means the Regional Secretary of Pringsewu Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus in Pringsewu Regency. 7. Woman means an adult human being of female gender. 8. Child means a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence means a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim means a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence means any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women means any act of violence against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children means any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence means any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence means any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner. 17. Neglect means the act of neglecting women and or children within the scope of the household which according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence means any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women means all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 20. Law enforcement means action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid means legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Implementation of protection means a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention means direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss as a result of the actions of others. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant means a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal aid for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

CHAPTER II

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect or recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to implement prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.
